evidence: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45 (Create) and :129 (Update) call d.recordLegacyDuration on a Storage.Create/Storage.Update failure, timed from startStorage, so storage failures are counted as legacy metrics. :166 (DeleteCollection goroutine) calls d.recordStorageDuration for the Legacy.DeleteCollection call timed from startLegacy, so legacy timings are counted as storage metrics. Delete (:103) and DeleteCollection (:156) record the storage error path correctly, which shows the other three are mistakes.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:51, :110, :135, :163: each goroutine builds its context with context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...), where ctx is the request context. net/http cancels a request's context once ServeHTTP returns, and the k8s apiserver handler returns the created/updated result right away (:59, :116, :143, :169). A child of that context is canceled at the same moment, so the async legacy write can be aborted before it finishes, which defeats the 'safe measure' described in the PR. Fix: use context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (Go 1.21+), which keeps the context values, then apply the 10s timeout. dualwriter_mode1.go:54 already had the same pattern before this PR, but mode 3 is new code.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106: d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage) passes the object name where every other call (e.g. :103, :113, :132) passes options.Kind. On success, Delete metrics are labeled per object name, which mislabels the kind dimension and gives the label unbounded cardinality.

pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:97: in Delete, ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log), while :96 built the enriched log with name/kind/method. Every other method uses the enriched log (:39, :66, :82, :123, :150). Loggers pulled from the context by the storage layers therefore lose the name/kind/method fields.

pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go: every mode-3 subtest (added at ~:132, :191, :287) enables featuremgmt.FlagKubernetesPlaylists. With that flag on, pkg/api/playlist.go:30-38 sends the legacy /api/playlists handlers through newPlaylistK8sHandler, i.e. the k8s client, so they go through DualWriterMode3.Get/List and read from unified storage (dualwriter_mode3.go:63-92), not from the legacy SQL store. The legacy-API checks in doPlaylistTests (the search at :523, getFromBothAPIs at :623) never read what the fire-and-forget legacy writes produce, so no race exists.
